A. Positive thinking leads a man to success. One who thinks that he can achieve the things will put his best to achieve.

B. Self-confidence, determination, perseverance, and hard work are the key factors of success.

C. He will not fetter by the problems in the path of success and one day he will win positively.

questions.solution:

• **Sentence A is the first sentence** as it sets the vision and current perspective:
 
 
• "Positive thinking leads a man to success. One who thinks that he can achieve the things will put his best to achieve."
 
 
 
• **Sentence C follows** as it highlights modern soft power assets, reflecting how this vision translates into contemporary influence:
 
 
• "He will not fetter by the problems in the path of success and one day he will win positively."
 
 
 
• **Sentence B is the third sentence** because it connects these modern influences with historical figures and the values they promoted:
 
 
• "Self-confidence, determination, perseverance, and hard work are the key factors of success."
 
 
 
• **Sentence D is the fourth** as it delves into the deep historical context, providing a foundation for the modern vision and influence:
 
 
• "Every small or big, easy, or complex problem has its solution. There is a way out of every labyrinth, there is an answer to every enigma."

"Positive thinking leads a man to success. One who thinks that he can achieve the things will put his best to achieve. He will not fetter by the problems in the path of success and one day he will win positively. Self-confidence, determination, perseverance, and hard work are the key factors of success. questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P. some experienced teachers say that

Q. teaching about English is easy and

R. teaching English is difficult as

S. the latter needs dedication, resources and many more
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (4)** i.e. **PQRS**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with "some experienced teachers say that," which is correctly indicated by **part (P).**
 
• It is followed by "teaching about English is easy and," which introduces the comparison, making **(Q)** the next logical part.
 
• Then, "teaching English is difficult as" follows, which logically contrasts the previous statement, making **(R)** the correct sequence.
 
• Finally, "the latter needs dedication, resources and many more" completes the sentence, explaining why teaching English is difficult, which is **(S).**

Therefore, the correct answer is **PQRS.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (PRSQ):** This order disrupts the logical flow, as it places "teaching English is difficult" before mentioning "teaching about English is easy," making the contrast unclear.
 
• **Option 2 (PSQR):** This order incorrectly places "the latter needs dedication, resources and many more" before the full explanation of why teaching English is difficult.
 
• **Option 3 (PSRQ):** This order is incorrect because it places "teaching English is difficult" too early, without first introducing the contrast.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

When is this car driven by you?

options.text: When did you drive this car?
When should you drive this car?
When do you drive this car?
When will you drive this car?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "When do you drive this car?"
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "this car" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "do drive" to "is driven" (present simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "you."
 
• Ensure the interrogative format is maintained.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"When do you drive this car?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"When did you drive this car?" – This changes the tense to past.
 
• **Option 2: **"When should you drive this car?" – This changes the modal verb.
 
• **Option 4: **"When will you drive this car?" – This changes the tense to future.

questions.solution:

• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:** "We" becomes "they" and "you" becomes "him."
 
• **Tense Change:** "were planning" becomes "had been planning" to reflect past continuous tense.
 
• **Time Change:** "next week" becomes "the following week."
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted to indirect speech.
 
• Quotation marks are removed.
 
• Appropriate tense and pronoun changes are made.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *They said that they had been planning to visit him the following week.*

• Incorrect tense "have been planning" does not match the past tense context.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** They said that they had planned to visit him next week.
 
 
• Incorrect tense "had planned" changes the meaning to a completed action rather than ongoing planning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** They said that they are planning to visit him the coming week.
